decision: Weight precision modes (full, balanced, compact) for the Metal engine: int8 and int4 kernels, a quantized weight cache file, measurements deciding what ships

decision: Metal wires a bound buffer in full on first use: binding a 4.6 GB mmapped shard with setBuffer alone raised the system wired count by 4.8 GB in 60 ms whatever the kernel read, and task_info footprint and resident_size did not move; the CPU page walk moved resident_size, not wired
why: the memory saving of a mode is the sum of the buffers it binds, so quantized modes must not bind the whole shards; the metric to report is the wired delta from host_statistics64, with task_info beside it
evidence: scratchpad wire_probe.swift output in the transcript (12:3x); vm_stat Pages wired down 464494 before, 748907 after
result: design: quantized modes bind the cache file plus page-aligned sub-buffers over the in-place tensors they still read

decision: Formats: int8 per row with fp16 scales in groups of 128 along K; int4 in groups of 64 with an fp16 scale and fp16 bias (w = s*q + b); experts re-quantized FP8 to the same int4; the router and the N<=256 projections stay bf16 in every mode; lm_head stored as its 4097 candidate rows; embeddings stay in place; small vectors are copied into the cache file; balanced keeps FP8 experts in place through sub-buffers over each layer's contiguous expert runs
why: fp16 scale error 2^-11 is an eighth of the int8 step at half the bytes of fp32; group 64 int4 costs 4.5 bits per weight against 5 for group 32 and decode is bandwidth bound; the narrow matrices are 1 percent of the bytes and gate routing and the recurrence; the shard scan showed each layer's experts in 2 to 4 contiguous runs
evidence: scratchpad/brief.md; scratchpad/shard_layout.py output in the transcript

decision: fp16 KV caches are not part of compact: at 1000 positions the 23 caches read 94 MB per frame against about 2.2 GB of weights (under 3 percent of the bytes) and hold 0.96 GB at full capacity (under 5 percent of the mode's wired memory), while they would need a second attention and kv_write kernel path plus tuner changes
why: the brief asked for them only if simple; the arithmetic says the gain is under the measurement noise
evidence: capacity 10240 x 23 layers x 2 KV heads x 256 x 4 B x 2
result: caches stay fp32 in every mode, to be said in the README

why: the benchmark checklist asks for the sentence before the run; the noise band comes from the existing reports

decision: Why the decode gain is below the byte saving (drama profile --rows 1): the dense projections shrink with their bytes (linear qkv 2.70, 1.59, 1.19 ms over 30 layers; tower 6.2 to 3.7 ms), the one-row expert kernels take 3.9, 3.8 and 3.5 ms in full, balanced and compact, so int4 experts return a tenth of their byte saving at one row, and router plus bucket (0.9 ms), norms and residuals (0.6), the GDN recurrence and conv (0.5), RoPE, attention and the sampler read no weights and stay the same; prefill is unchanged in every mode
why: the benchmark checklist asks for the limiter before a number is reported
result: named in the README; the one-row expert kernels are the next place to look if compact is ever to earn its bytes

decision: balanced ships as an Advanced option (within the seed-to-seed band of full on WER and speaker similarity, 26 percent less GPU time per decode frame against the 20 percent bar; memory 9 percent less, under the 25 percent bar, because the FP8 experts stay); compact stays in the enum as experimental (ModelPrecisionMode.isExperimental true): speaker similarity below every seed of full, teacher-forced error four to five times the bf16 oracle's, no eos in five of five reference-chunking runs; full stays the default
